title: Several conditions

cells.text: Sometimes one condition isn't enough, like "players from the USA **with** more than 400 hours". This lesson shows how to combine conditions.

cells.prompt: Press Run to load the players table.
cells.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv("players.csv")
df.head()

cells.text: `&` means **AND**: both conditions must be true. Each condition goes in its **own round brackets**, then the whole thing goes inside `df[ ]`: `df[(condition 1) & (condition 2)]`.

cells.prompt: Press Run to show players from the USA with more than 400 hours.
How many players are from Japan AND have more than 50 hours? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: `|` means **OR**: at least one condition must be true. It's the straight line key, usually above Enter (Shift + \). It needs the same round brackets.

cells.prompt: Replace ___ with the OR sign so players from Japan OR Brazil show, then press Run.
hints: OR is the straight line |, not the letter l or I.

cells.prompt: Your turn: show players from the USA with fewer than 400 hours. Both must be true, so use &, and keep each condition in its own round brackets.

cells.text: To match any value from a list, `isin()` is a shortcut for lots of `|`. `df[df["country"].isin(["Japan", "UK"])]` keeps players from Japan or the UK. Notice the list in square brackets inside the round ones.

cells.prompt: Press Run to show players from Japan or the UK.
Show players from Japan, Mexico or the Philippines, using isin().
hints: Copy the cell above and put 3 countries in the list.

cells.text: The most common mistake here is forgetting the round brackets around each condition.

cells.prompt: This code has no round brackets around the conditions. What will happen? Pick one, then press Run.

cells.text: Python works out `&` **before** `==` and `>`, so without brackets it tries to combine the wrong pieces and fails. Whenever you see an error with & or |, check the brackets first.

recap: & means AND (both true), | means OR (either true), and each condition needs its own round brackets. isin() matches any value from a list.
